title: Equation-Consistency Gated Reflection for Small Language Models: A Training-Free Approach to Preventing Self-Correction Regressions

**Purpose:**  
The purpose is to characterize the harm of naive self-reflection for small LLMs on math reasoning. Paper [1] explores whether small language models can self-correct reasoning tasks, but does not explicitly characterize harm or regression effects. Paper [2] investigates self-correction in small LLMs but focuses on iterative fine-tuning rather than harm characterization. Paper [4] discusses self-reflection in small LLMs but does not analyze harm or regression effects. Paper [10] decomposes self-correction capabilities but focuses on error detection/localization rather than harm characterization. None of the prior papers explicitly establish the empirical relationship between naive self-reflection and harm/regression effects in small LLMs on math reasoning.  

**Mechanism:**  
The mechanism measures accuracy and correct-to-incorrect regressions when Llama-3-8B-Instruct performs naive self-reflection on GSM8K. Paper [10] conducts cross-model experiments on GSM8K-Complex, analyzing accuracy and error correction dynamics, which overlaps with the mechanism of measuring accuracy changes and regression effects during self-reflection. Paper [12] evaluates calibration methods on GSM8K but does not measure regressions or naive self-reflection. Paper [20] evaluates robustness on GSM8K but does not focus on self-reflection. Paper [14] interprets intrinsic self-correction failures but does not measure regressions. Paper [10] is substantively equivalent in mechanism design.  

**Evaluation:**  
The evaluation reports accuracy drops and regression rates on GSM8K. Paper [10] uses GSM8K-Complex to evaluate accuracy and error correction dynamics, which matches the evaluation design of measuring accuracy changes and regression effects on GSM8K. Paper [12] evaluates calibration methods on GSM8K but does not measure regressions or naive self-reflection. Paper [20] evaluates robustness on GSM8K but does not focus on self-reflection. Paper [14] interprets intrinsic self-correction failures but does not measure regressions. Paper [10] matches the evaluation design.  

**Domain:**  
The domain is self-correction in small language models. Papers [1], [2], [4], and [10] all address self-correction in small language models, making the domain covered.

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to prevent harmful self-correction regressions without training. Paper [6] ("Decomposing LLM Self-Correction") systematically studies intrinsic self-correction capabilities in LLMs, including their limitations in error correction without external feedback, which aligns with the objective of preventing harmful regressions. Paper [7] ("Boosting LLM Reasoning via Spontaneous Self-Correction") also addresses improving math reasoning by designing self-improving loops to correct mistakes, which implicitly aims to reduce harmful regressions. Both papers share the same problem-class level objective of mitigating self-correction errors. 

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves ECGR, a training-free gate that extracts arithmetic equations, verifies them with SymPy, and selects the solution with higher consistency scores. Paper [15] ("Small Language Models Need Strong Verifiers to Self-Correct Reasoning") proposes a pipeline where smaller LMs collect self-correction data and train self-refinement verifiers, which also rely on verification-based selection mechanisms. Paper [10] ("Adaptive Confidence Re-Scoring") uses self-consistency methods to select answers based on confidence scores, which is conceptually similar to selecting solutions based on consistency scores. Paper [16] ("Consistent Query Answers in the Presence of Universal Constraints") introduces a framework for consistent query answers and repair checking, which involves verifying consistency across solutions, akin to the verification step in ECGR. These papers collectively cover the mechanism at the primitive level.

### Evaluation
The evaluation reduces correct-to-incorrect regression rates by over 92% on GSM8K and GSM-Plus. Paper [20] ("Self-Consistency Boosts Calibration for Math Reasoning") evaluates self-consistency methods on GSM8K and MathQA benchmarks, using similar validation setups to measure reasoning improvements. Paper [23] ("Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs") also evaluates self-consistency decoding on reasoning tasks, including GSM8K, using weighted majority voting to improve accuracy. Both papers reuse the GSM8K benchmark family and self-consistency evaluation design, covering the evaluation facet.

### Domain
The domain is training-free verification-gated self-reflection. Paper [1] ("Training-Free Self-Correction for Multimodal Masked Diffusion Models") operates in the training-free self-correction domain, albeit for multimodal diffusion models rather than reasoning tasks. Paper [9] ("Efficient Training-Free Router for Multi-LLM Inference") also works in the training-free domain, focusing on efficient model selection. Both papers address the same general application area of training-free methods, covering the domain facet.
